English

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Hyphenation: tiers
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)

Noun

[edit]

tiers

  1. plural of tier

Verb

[edit]

tiers

  1. third-person singular simple present indicative of tier

Anagrams

  • Istre, Reist, Siret, Sirte, iters, reist, resit, rites, tires, tries

tiers c

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old French tiers, terce, tierz, tierce, from Latin tertius.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /tjɛʁ/
  • Audio; “un tiers”:(file)
  • Audio (France (Agen)):(file)

Adjective

[edit]

French Wikipedia article on 3

tiers (feminine tierce, masculine plural tiers, feminine plural tierces)

  1. (dated) third
  2. third-party

Synonyms

[edit]
  • (third): troisième

Derived terms

[edit]
  • tiers-monde

Noun

[edit]
French numbers (edit)
[a], [b] ←  2 3 4  → 
    Cardinal: trois
    Ordinal: troisième
    Ordinal abbreviation: 3e, (nonstandard) 3ème
    Multiplier: triple
    Fractional: tiers
French Wikipedia article on 3

tiers m (invariable)

  1. a third (one of three equal parts)
  2. a third-party (an outsider of a group)

Further reading

[edit]
  • “tiers”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Anagrams

[edit]

  • tierce (all attested with both masculine and feminine nouns)

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin tertius.

Adjective

[edit]

tiers m (occasionally used with feminine nouns)

  1. third (3rd)
